The G7 circuit breaker operates on the principle of detecting drift in prediction model calibration using the Murphy (1973) Brier decomposition. It compares ECE over short (30-sample) and long (250-sample) windows to identify deviations. The core operator ΔECE = ECE₃₀ − ECE₂₅₀ is compared against a fixed threshold θ = 0.02. However, due to inherent binomial fluctuations, the expected ECE difference under perfect calibration is positive and bounded by the noise floor σ = √(p(1−p)/N), leading to an expected ΔECE ≈ √(2/π)·σ. This implies that even calibrated families may trigger halts unless a correction is applied. The failure mode arises from applying the rule per sample rather than per family, causing incorrect classification of stable models. The correct application requires grouping samples by family and applying the corrected threshold (bias + 2σ) to avoid false positives. The system must also account for the fact that the spec’s original number (0.02) is a component of the final threshold, not a standalone criterion.
